script.base: No priced favorite, so script is inferred from two games only. Carolina is pass-leaning: Jalen Coker and Tetairoa McMillan each have 18 targets (Coker 204 yards on 172 air; McMillan 176 yards on 251 air), with Chuba Hubbard the only real rusher at 22 carries for 102 yards (4.6 YPC) and Jonathan Brooks 9/30 plus A.J. Dillon 8/25 behind him. Cleveland cannot run inside: Quinshon Judkins 24/54 (2.25 YPC) while Deshaun Watson has 11/62 on the ground and Denzel Boston has the explosives (11 targets, 154 yards, 174 air). Base flow is competitive, not a blowout: Carolina throws into a Browns defense that blitzes only 19% (Bryce Young EPA/db 0.37 not blitzed vs 0.18 blitzed) and has leaked the middle (10.1 YPA on 10 throws) plus 7 passes of 20+. Cleveland mixes stalled interior runs with Watson scrambles and short throws because Carolina blitzes 44% (Cleveland EPA/db -0.20 vs blitz, +0.27 vs none) and is missing two linebackers.
script.flip1: Cleveland finally runs it. Carolina has allowed 6.31 YPC and 8 runs of 10+, and LBs Devin Lloyd (calf) and Claudin Cherelus (shoulder) are out, so Judkins carries spike, Watson keeps scrambling, Cleveland holds the ball, and Carolina pass volume stalls if they are not trailing. That kills McMillan/Coker/Waller yardage and kills Judkins receiving. Teven Jenkins (back) being out is what makes this flip less likely than the defensive holes imply.
script.flip2: Shootout if the compromised secondaries play out: Carolina S Nick Scott is out, Cleveland S Grant Delpit (shoulder) and CB Tyson Campbell (ankle) are questionable. Both dropback games stay live, Boston and McMillan clear, and a run-clock under story dies. Unsaved wind/rain could invert this into a slog; that forecast is not in the pack.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC or man/zone charting in the pack. Shell is inferred only. Cleveland blitzes 19% (passive). Carolina blitzes 44%. Location splits stand in for coverage: Cleveland YPA left 7.09 (23 throws), middle 10.1 (10), right 6.79 (24). Carolina YPA left 8.22 (18), middle 6.59 (17), right 5.92 (26).
matchup.pressure: Cleveland pressure is the low-blitz look: Young is better when not blitzed (EPA/db 0.37 vs 0.18), so Carolina deep and intermediate throws are live. Carolina pressure is the problem for Cleveland: EPA/db -0.20 when blitzed vs +0.27 when not, and Jenkins is out, so expect more quick throws and fewer clean deep shots. That boosts RB/TE catches and threatens Boston's 174 air yards even with Scott out.
matchup.bleeds: Cleveland bleeds explosives (7 passes of 20+ on 61) and the middle (10.1 YPA, small sample of 10). Rush defense is ordinary-leaky at 4.93 YPC with 9 runs of 10+, not a wall and not Carolina's 6.31 YPC mess. Carolina bleeds the run and the left side (8.22 YPA) and has two linebackers plus a safety out; they have allowed only 4 passes of 20+ on 66, so the give is underneath and on the ground more than a proven deep sieve.
matchup.overlap: Carolina's co-primary McMillan (18 targets, 251 air, 29% of listed targets) overlaps Cleveland's explosive-pass leak and the low-blitz environment, not a charted corner. Waller (5 targets, 61 yards, 34 air) is the middle-of-field candidate but the efficiency looks fluky. Cleveland's overlap with Carolina's weak spot is the run and the linebacker level, which would be Judkins rushing — except Jenkins is out and Judkins is at 2.25 YPC, so the cleaner overlap is Judkins as a checkdown (7 targets, 44 yards, -7 air) against a 44% blitz and two missing linebackers.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both leans lost. McMillan: Campbell and Delpit both played, Cleveland took away the 20+ shots, and the 251 air yards turned into another pile of incompletions, finishing near 45-55 yards; or Carolina got ahead, Hubbard went from 11 carries to a clock-killing load, and the passing game never needed a second explosive. The 75-yard game shows he can clear without a 100-yard outlier, but a shadow plus a run script is enough to lose 62.5. Judkins: Cleveland gashed the 6.31 YPC defense and the backup linebackers on the ground, Jenkins' absence did not force checkdowns, Judkins ran 18 times for modest yards and saw one target, and Sanders took the swing that was worth 25 yards in one of the first two games. The 17-yard game was already only 3.5 yards over the number, so the counter-case is real. It is not stronger than the read, because the blitz rate, the two linebacker absences and the guard absence are all in the pre-kick report and both games cleared 13.5, so the lean stays and is not upgraded to strong.
slip_story: Do not parlay these two. They are not one story. McMillan belongs to a Carolina-pass slip against a low-blitz defense that leaks explosives; the natural partners (Waller, Coker) failed the fluky-efficiency screen, the questionable tag, or the missing price, so he is a standalone lean. Judkins receiving belongs to a Cleveland-checkdown slip against Carolina's blitz and missing linebackers; Fannin (21 and 54) and Concepcion (43 and 28) did not clear form, and Boston over would need the opposite of the pressure story, so he is also standalone. A Cleveland run-clock win hits neither the same way: McMillan can still eat if Carolina trails, while Judkins receiving dies. Keep them off the same ticket. No third leg, no TD, no depth receiver, no mix with a total under. No bet is placed.
